title: Enterprise Metric Ownership and Alert Routing Cookbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This cookbook defines a pragmatic, repeatable approach for mapping customer-visible telemetry to clear owners, creating routing rules in our alerting stack, and operationalizing those alerts inside Customer Success (CS) and Engineering workflows. It is intended for CS onboarding leads, SREs, and product owners who need consistent, auditable alerts that drive fast, customer-facing outcomes.

Scope: applies to all enterprise tenants (hosted, dedicated, private) and the following telemetry sources: telemetry-gateway, redwood-proxy, model-router, kvcache-service, embeddings-indexer. This doc focuses on customer-impacting metrics (latency, error-rate, cost-anomaly, model-quality regression) rather than internal infra-only metrics.

Owner and Contact

- Primary owner: Customer Success Observability (team-ops-cs-observability)
- Secondary owner: Eng SRE (team-sre-platform)
- Oncall escalation: Eng SRE PagerDuty (PD: team-sre-platform)

Definitions and Goal Metrics

- Customer-visible metric: any metric or log pattern that maps to a customer SLA, feature, or billing impact (examples below).
- Severity tiers and target time-to-ack (TTA):
  - Sev P0 (Critical): customer-facing outage, >5% of tenant traffic impacted or entire tenant unreachable — TTA: 15 minutes
  - Sev P1 (High): degraded experience (latency or increased error rate) for a production route — TTA: 60 minutes
  - Sev P2 (Medium): cost anomaly or single-model quality regression flagged by evaluations — TTA: 8 hours
  - Sev P3 (Low): informational alerts, trend warnings for QBR — TTA: 72 hours

Metric-to-Owner Matrix (examples)

| Metric name | Observable source | Owner team | Default severity | Notes |
|-------------|-------------------|------------|------------------|-------|
| request.p50.latency| telemetry-gateway | team-sre-platform | P1 | If tenant p50 increases > 2x baseline for >10m |
| request.error_rate | redwood-proxy | team-sre-platform | P0 | If error_rate > 5% for a tenant and sustained |
| embed.indexing.lag | embeddings-indexer | team-data-ops | P1 | Backpressure on indexer affecting search freshness |
| kvcache.kv_miss_rate | kvcache-service | team-serving-runtime | P1 | Rapid rise correlates with token spend increase |
| model.quality.regression.alpha | model-router/evals | team-applied-ml | P2 | Triggered by evaluation harness comparing model vN to baseline |
| tenant.cost.per_hour | billing-collector | customer-success | P2 | Sudden cost > 3x expected forecast |

Alert Routing and Naming Conventions

- Alert name format: cs.<tenant>.<service>.<metric>.<severity>. Example: cs.acme-corp.redis-proxy.request-error-rate.P0
- Tags/labels to include: tenant_id, customer_tier (enterprise/dedicated/private), region, route, last_deployed_model, runbook_id
- Recommended Slack channels: #cs-alerts (triage), #sre-ops (escalation), #cust-<tenant_short> (customer-specific comms if enabled)

Routing Rules (examples)

1) Immediate P0 routing
   - Condition: alert severity == P0 AND tenant.tier == enterprise
   - Action: page Eng SRE PD (team-sre-platform) AND notify #cs-alerts Slack channel. Create CS incident in Zendesk with priority urgent.
2) P1 automated triage
   - Condition: severity == P1 AND first_alert_count >= 3 in 30m
   - Action: create short-lived support ticket assigned to CS Observability, attach grafana dashboard and recent traces. If no ack in 60m, escalate to Eng SRE PD.
3) Cost/Quality P2 handling
   - Condition: metric in {tenant.cost.per_hour, model.quality.regression.alpha}
   - Action: assign to CS FinOps or Applied ML respectively; auto-generate customer notification draft for review.

Alert Payload Example (YAML for routing system)

---
alert_name: "cs.{{tenant}}.telemetry-gateway.p50.latency.P1"
tenant: "{{tenant}}"
threshold: "p50 > baseline*2 for >10m"
owner: "team-sre-platform"
pagerduty: "team-sre-platform"
slack_channels: ["#cs-alerts", "#sre-ops"]
runbook_id: "rr-metric-p50-latency-v1"

Runbook: p50 latency spike (rr-metric-p50-latency-v1)

1) Verify the scope
   - Query: Grafana dashboard: Dashboard ID: cs-onboarding/latency-summary. Apply tenant filter = <tenant_id> and route filter = <route>.
   - Confirm whether spike is single region or cross-region and whether multiple tenants are affected.
2) Quick mitigations (first 30 min)
   - If proxy CPU > 85%: scale proxy pool (kubectl scale deploy proxy --replicas=+2 for dedicated pools).
   - If model hot-sharding: switch route to fallback model variant (use model-router override API: POST /v1/admin/overrides).
   - If KV cache miss storm: temporarily enable cache-skim mode (feature flag: kvcache.skim=true) for tenant.
3) Deeper triage (30m–4h)
   - Collect flamegraphs (perf profiler), recent traces (x-trace-id), and last 6 hours of redeploy events.
   - Correlate with release tags: last_deployed_model and infra-deploy-id.
4) Communication
   - Customer comms template (initial):
     Subject: "[Redwood] Brief outage affecting <feature> for <tenant>"
     Body: "We are investigating elevated latency impacting <route>. Initial mitigation steps are in progress. We will update within 60 minutes with next steps. Owner: <owner_name> (CS). Escalation: Eng SRE oncall."

Onboarding Checklist for New Enterprise Tenants (observability handoff)

- Before prod cutover:
  1. Ensure tenant metadata is registered in the telemetry-gateway (tenant_id, billing_code, support_contacts).
  2. Validate tenant-specific dashboards exist (latency, error-rate, cost, model-quality) and are shared with CS and SRE.
  3. Add tenant to alert routing rules with correct owner and Slack channels.
  4. Confirm PagerDuty escalation path is present and tested (test page with PD test key).
  5. Run a synthetic journey (see synthetic-journey-sla-calibration-playbook) and confirm alerts are not noisy.

Operational Playflows

- Normal triage (P1/P2): CS Observability owns first-touch. Use the CS triage checklist inside the Zendesk ticket: attach dashboards, record mitigation actions, propose next steps (mitigate, rollback, model-swap, capacity increase).
- Immediate escalation (P0): Eng SRE paged immediately. CS takes ownership of customer communication cadence and QBR action items.
- Post-incident: create an RCA within 48 hours if incident severity >= P1 and affected revenue or >10 customers. Assign action owners with due dates and track in the QBR.

Noise Reduction and Alert Health

- Weekly review: CS Observability runs an alert hygiene sweep every Monday: remove stale alerts, update thresholds based on tenant baselines, and collapse duplicate alerts across services.
- Signal-to-noise metric: track alerts_per_week_per_tenant and target < 3 actionable alerts/week for enterprise. If exceeded, assign an action to reduce.

Integration snippets and examples

1) Grafana dashboard sharing (CLI snippet)
   - grafana-cli dashboard export 12345 > acme-latency-dash.json
   - grafana-cli dashboard import --folder "Tenants/Acme" acme-latency-dash.json
2) Routing rule (example JSON for alert manager):
   {
     "match": {"tenant":"acme-corp","severity":"P1"},
     "route_to": ["team-sre-platform","channel:#cs-alerts"],
     "suppress_if": {"maintenance_mode":true}
   }

Customer Communication Templates

- 60-minute update (short)
  - Subject: "Update: ongoing issue affecting <feature> — <tenant>"
  - Body: "Summary: elevated latency persisted affecting <route>. Mitigation: scaled proxy and switched to fallback model. Next update in 2 hours or sooner. Contact: <cs_owner>@redwood.ai"

- Post-incident summary (example)
  - Subject: "Incident report: <short-id> — impact summary and remediation"
  - Body: "What happened, Customer impact, Timeline of mitigations, Root cause (investigating/identified), Actions taken, Preventative actions and expected timeline for completion."

SLO and Escalation thresholds (customer-facing)

- Availability: 99.95% per month for hosted Tier 1 routes. Escalate to P0 when availability drops below 99.5% in a rolling 1h window.
- Latency: p95 < 450ms. Escalate to P1 when p95 > 900ms for >10 minutes.
- Error rate: <1% across tenant traffic. Escalate to P0 when error rate >5% for >5 minutes.

Governance, Reporting, and QBR Inputs

- Each month CS Observability exports the following artifacts for QBRs: top 3 incidents for the tenant, alert burn rate, cost anomalies detected, model quality deltas.
- Action ownership: every alert that results in an RCA must have an owner and a completion date recorded in the quarter backlog.

Appendices

A. Common mitigations quick list
- Scale dedicated pools, swap to model-variant, enable cache-skim, temporary rate-limiting per-tenant, rollback last infra deploy.

B. Useful links
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/cs-onboarding/latency-summary
- PagerDuty: https://pd.redwood.internal/services/team-sre-platform
- Runbook repo: docs/runbooks/rr-metric-p50-latency-v1

C. Change log
- 2025-09-12: Document created by Maya Chen (CS Observability).
- 2026-02-10: Updated severity TTA targets and added cost anomaly routing (reviewers: Julian Park, Lena Novak).

If you have questions or need a tenant added to routing rules, open a ticket to #cs-ops-requests with payload: tenant_id, owner_email, desired_channels.
